decision needed: Decided (Jeff 2026-11-24): a NIBRS-only figure over years that start before 2017 is answered from 2017 with a line, instead of declining with a "From 2017" button.
situation (example wording): "carjacking rates in Atlanta for the past ten years", "drug offenses in Salem since 2000", "aggravated assault with a firearm in DC and Prince George's since 2010", "violent crime by offender age, California, 2015 to 2025" (a measure only NIBRS holds, with no yearly Crime Index figure, over a period that starts before NIBRS's first year)
what the app does today: A decline ("NIBRS figures here cover January 2017 through ..., so they don't include ...") with a button, "From 2017, the first year in the data" (Jeff 2026-11-02). Arrests alone were answered from 2017 with a line (Jeff 2026-11-11).
proposed behavior: Answered from 2017, with one line after the title: "These figures come from NIBRS, which starts in 2017, so 2015 to 2016 aren't included." ("2016 isn't included." for one year). The same line the arrests rule uses, with "These figures" for "Arrests here". Not used when Crime Index has a yearly figure for the same question (that offer stays), when the question is monthly for one agency (the span choices stay), or when the years are a list.
exact default or choices offered: The answer from 2017, with the line.
why: The labels for these questions are answers (R14); the arrests rule already answers this way. The button asked for a second click to get what the question was after.
status: Accepted 2026-11-24 (Jeff: "Adopt for now, we will add 1991 to 2016 pre launch"). NIBRS coverage for 1991 to 2016 is planned before launch, and this rule's cut-off year will move then. The start year is read from the release (release.firstMonth) in one place, never written into the rule's code or wording.
test cases: scripts/test-nibrs-shadow.ts ("A period starting before the data": Shoplifting in Memphis per year from 2012 to 2020; the forecast alternative, "Will shoplifting go up in Memphis next year?").
